chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, "If some event occurs, and Allah does not show me that, then whom should I follow as Imam?" So he gestured toward his son Mūsā.
He said: I said, "Then if an event happens to Mūsā, whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son."
I said, "Then if an event happens to his son, and he leaves behind an elder brother and a young son, then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son, then one after another."
And in the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: "Then it is like this forever."

key_terms.أَئْتَمُّ: to take someone as Imam and follow his authority
key_terms.بِوَلَدِهِ: through his son; indicating succession to the son
key_terms.مُوسَى: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, identified here as the next Imam
key_terms.وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا: one after another in continuous succession

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the continuation of the Imamate among the descendants of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imamate continues through the descendant of the Imam, passing from son to son in succession. It also clarifies that the authority does not return to an elder brother when a son is present, affirming hereditary continuity within the designated line of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
